steps.why: The engine as a library: a C program evaluates an expression with it.

steps.script: printf '%s\n' '#include <quickjs.h>' 'int main(void) { JSRuntime *runtime = JS_NewRuntime(); JSContext *context = JS_NewContext(runtime); int answer = 0; JS_ToInt32(context, &answer, JS_Eval(context, "6 * 7", 5, "amy", JS_EVAL_TYPE_GLOBAL)); JS_FreeContext(context); JS_FreeRuntime(runtime); return answer != 42; }' > /tmp/amy-quickjs.c && cc -O0 /tmp/amy-quickjs.c -lquickjs -o /tmp/amy-quickjs && /tmp/amy-quickjs

steps.why: Janis as a library: a C program that is one script, linked on the engine that janis installs.

steps.script: echo 'import { readFileSync } from "node:fs"; process.exitCode = readFileSync(process.argv[2], "utf8").length;' > /tmp/amy-embed.mjs && printf '%s\n' '#include <dolly/quickjs-runner.h>' 'int main(int argc, char **argv) { return dolly_quickjs_run(argc, argv, "/tmp/amy-embed.mjs"); }' > /tmp/amy-embed.c && cc -O0 /tmp/amy-embed.c -ldolly-js -lquickjs -o /tmp/amy-embed && printf 12345 > /tmp/amy-embed.txt; /tmp/amy-embed /tmp/amy-embed.txt; test $? = 5

steps.why: tsc is Janis started on the compiler: the package installs janis, and janis the engine it is built on. tsc compiles and janis runs.

steps.script: cd /tmp && echo 'export const answer: number = 6 * 7; console.log(answer);' > amy-answer.ts && tsc --target ES2023 --module ES2022 amy-answer.ts && test "$(janis amy-answer.js)" = 42 && amy list | grep -q '^janis  *installed ' && amy list | grep -q '^quickjs  *installed ' && man tsc > /dev/null

steps.why: The engine's own command: it evaluates, and holds no module of Node's.
A Node-style script reads a file. Janis starts its children with sh, which posix holds.

steps.script: echo read > /tmp/amy-janis.txt && test "$(janis -e 'console.log(require("node:fs").readFileSync("/tmp/amy-janis.txt", "utf8").trim().toUpperCase())')" = READ && test "$(janis -e 'console.log(require("node:child_process").execSync("echo spawned").toString().trim())')" = spawned && man janis > /dev/null && ! command -v tsc

steps.why: janis-install brings the commands it starts, janis, gzip and sbase's; without the registry it refuses a git spec by name.

steps.script: man janis-install > /dev/null && command -v sha512sum > /dev/null && ! janis-install user/repo 2> /dev/null
